source.title: Confidence Regulation Neurons in Language Models
source.authors: Alessandro Stolfo; Ben Wu; Wes Gurnee; Yonatan Belinkov; Xing-Yi Song; Mrinmaya Sachan; Neel Nanda

page_placements.theme: Downstream readers of induction heads: entropy neurons and repetition neurons

record.tranche_reason: The study uses induction heads as an intervention in a case study of confidence regulation, but does not test their formation, copying behavior, training-time transition, or role in in-context or few-shot learning.
record.gate_note: The paper defines induction heads and selects them using prefix-matching scores, but those definitions and selection scores are not reported as tests of the claim. It measures how head interventions and attributions relate to entropy-neuron activity during repeated sequences; it does not measure induction-head formation over training or the claimed loss-based in-context-learning gain.
record.test_reason: The paper takes induction heads (selected by prefix-matching score, GPT-2 Small L5H1, L5H5, L6H9) as a given tool and measures how ablating them changes final-layer entropy-neuron activations. It does not measure induction-head formation, composition with previous-token heads, training dynamics, or the share of in-context learning they carry. Loss and entropy do fall on the repeated half of sequences (Fig. 5a), but this is not attributed to induction heads in a way that tests any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors show that entropy neurons raise output entropy (hedging) during induction, with clip-ablation of 11.2378 cutting entropy by up to 70%. BOS ablations show induction heads causally drive these neurons. The authors call the evidence for an 'induction-has-occurred' signal preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: Studies downstream confidence regulation in repeated-sequence settings using BOS ablations, mean attention-output ablations, and direct feature attribution; it does not reproduce training-time induction-head formation or the original in-context-learning/loss measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Head identity and ablation type affect the reported entropy-neuron response; for neuron 11.2870, the BOS-ablation effect changes direction between the start and remainder of the repeated sequence.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 Small, BOS-ablating induction head L5H1 sharply lowers entropy neuron 11.2378 activation (to ~4). Adding L5H5 and L6H9 lowers it further, while random heads have little effect. Direct attribution suggests the effect is largely mediated by L11H8 and the layer 8–10 MLPs, except for neuron 11.2870.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction heads emit a generic 'induction-occurred' signal that downstream entropy neurons use to hedge confidence during repeated text.

record.problems: The induction case study is limited to GPT-2 Small. The authors characterize the head–neuron interaction evidence as preliminary; several results are qualitative or figure-based, and direct attribution does not establish the full intervening circuit.
record.rows_left_out: No additional induction-head-related outcomes were left out. General entropy-neuron and token-frequency-neuron analyses were not included because they do not measure the induction-head claim.

untested.parts: No test of previous-token-head composition or of the [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying itself. Heads are only selected by prefix-matching score.
No training checkpoints, so no test of abrupt formation or a loss bump.
No attribution of in-context loss reduction to induction heads.
Induction heads are identified only in GPT-2 Small. The cross-model results concern entropy neurons, not induction heads.
No manipulation of data or training setup affecting induction heads. The dropout result concerns the unembedding null space.

record.verdict_notes: The gating decision is T4/uses_without_test: the study uses induction heads as an instrument, and its rows concern entropy-neuron responses, so none bear on V1–V7. Entropy-neuron universality across models (GPT-2, Pythia, Phi-2, Gemma, LLaMA2) is about entropy neurons, not induction heads, and does not bear on V4.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test formation by composing with a previous-token head, nor whether the heads implement the [A][B] … [A] → [B] copying behavior.
No training-time formation measurement, sharp in-context-learning gain, or corresponding loss-curve bump is tested.
Does not measure induction heads as the mechanism behind most in-context learning in large transformers.
Does not assess induction behavior across model families, sizes, training runs, architectures, or modalities.
Does not vary data or training setup to test induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Does not test few-shot task learning or compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of that learning.
Does not track formation sub-steps or overlapping transitions during training.

relation.reason: BOS and mean-output ablations test effects on entropy neurons, rather than induction-head formation, copying, training transitions, universality, or contribution to most in-context learning.

tranche.reason: The study uses identified induction heads to investigate downstream confidence regulation. Its activation and attribution results do not test any listed induction-head claim version.

source_check.notes: Row states describe downstream activation effects and controls, not evidence for V1–V7. The generic induction signal and its proposed mediating circuit remain preliminary.
